subject: private_first_infantry_1812

shot.build: stage, tree 275e17456 + 8 uncommitted figure file(s): T-3553 round 4 in progress (the legwear pass in human-regulars.js and human-tailor-1835.js, and the other round-4 passes' working copies)

silhouette.what: Silhouette and fit of the clothes
silhouette.note: Owner ruling 2026-11-17: "i think against the regulars? they are probably closer to a regular and would have been outfitted with uniform?" The private is judged against the record of the U.S. regulars (us_1812_rules_and_articles_albany, the 1802 issue; us_1814_military_laws_and_regulations, the 1813 change read backwards); the pictures stay as period context for silhouette, the record (text) governs pattern. Against that record he reads as a regular: a blue coat with red collar and cuffs, white tape on the eight breast button holes (inferred from "trimmed with tape on the collar only"), skirts drawn down to a hand above the knee (inferred from "all the rank and file will wear coatees"; the length follows Ogden's silhouette), white crossbelts, white linen overalls, a felt cap with a feather. Round 4: the overalls are now cut close to the leg as both pictures draw legwear (Krimmel's pantaloons and gaiters, Ogden's gaiters): at 3 m the legs read as the knee and calf under the linen, closing on the half gaiters over the shoe, no longer the straight wide workwear tube. The record names linen overalls and half gaiters but not their cut; the close cut is inferred from the pictures, its amount (about 1-1.5 cm off the leg at LOD0) reconstructed. The thigh was already close and is unchanged; no buttons or strap under the shoe are drawn.

folds.note: The close overalls show the knee and calf through the linen, with few folds; at the hem they spread over the heel of the shoe in a short step rather than a smooth gaiter line (a few pixels at 3 m). The longer tails hang flat behind and part over the trailing leg mid-stride (human-skirt.js), no leg showing through them or through the overalls standing or walking (tools/test_human_regulars.mjs).

hat_hair.note: A tall black felt cap with a white feather, as the regulars' record read backwards (the 1813 change substituted leather for felt and pompons for feathers). Krimmel's volunteers wear bearskins and crested hats, Ogden's 1802-1810 men crested round hats; under the ruling the record governs, and the cap's cylinder shape stays reconstructed.

skin.note: Coloured pictures; a reconstructed face, no likeness of Paul Grummo is known.

hands.note: Bare at the sides on the stage; no musket here (the garrison's men carry theirs by duty, human-garrison.js; the pictures' men shoulder muskets).

stance.what: How the figure stands or sits
stance.note: Upright at attention in the rank; Krimmel's men stand the same way.

motion.note: A plain walk; the longer tails swing and part behind, the cartridge box rides the right hip.

differences.picture: Orange-red facings down the breast and a high faced collar (Krimmel's volunteers, 1811-13); faced lapels on Ogden's 1802-10 coats (1888 reconstruction).
differences.ours: Plain blue single-breasted breast, red only at collar and cuffs, as the regulars' record has it (the 1813 change took away "red collars or cuffs", nothing on the breast); a white tape loop on each of the eight breast button holes, from the button toward the wearer's left, inferred from "no lace shall be worn by any grade ... The button holes of these will be trimmed with tape on the collar only" (the form, length, white and one-sided loop reconstructed).

differences.picture: Close-fitting blue pantaloons and black gaiters to the knee (Krimmel); gaiters (Ogden).
differences.ours: White linen overalls to the shoe, as the record issues them ("two pair of woollen and two pair linen overalls", linen for August); the half gaiters ("one pair of half gaiters") stand under them as the black shoe.

differences.picture: Legwear cut close to the leg in both pictures.
differences.ours: Cut close to the leg at parse (human-regulars.js, round 4): about 1.8 cm off the knee, 1.4 off the calf and 2.3 above the ankle over the half gaiters at LOD0 (the shell drew 3.6, 1.9 and 5.0), the thigh as drawn (1.3). The record names overalls, not their cut: the close cut is inferred from the two pictures, its amount reconstructed. No buttons up the outside of the leg and no strap under the shoe are drawn; the far levels (LOD2-3) are narrower than drawn but looser than LOD0.
White crossbelts crossing mid-chest; the record gives no colour.

differences.picture: Short coats with white turnbacks on the tails (Krimmel's volunteers); long-skirted coats to the knee (Ogden).
differences.ours: Tails drawn down from mid-thigh (0.71 m off the ground) to a hand above the knee (0.56 m), plain blue, no turnbacks: longer than the coatee the 1813 change brought in ("all the rank and file will wear coatees"), inferred; the length is reconstructed, between the coatee and the officer's skirts at the bend of the knee, after Ogden's silhouette. Turnbacks are in neither record read for a private.

differences.picture: Bearskin caps and crested round hats (Krimmel); crested round hats with a feather (Ogden).
differences.ours: Tall black felt cylinder cap, white feather: felt and feather from the record read backwards.

differences.picture: Not legible in either picture; the record: the coatee's button holes "trimmed with tape on the collar only", so the collar carried tape before 1813 as after.
differences.ours: No tape on the collar: the exported collar falls to a centimetre or less at the front where its loops would sit. A loop of a few centimetres on the red, a few pixels at 3 m.
Cartridge box and scabbard at the right hip; no musket on the stage (the garrison's men carry theirs by duty).

differences.picture: High faced collar, a black stock (Krimmel).
differences.ours: High red collar over a black leather stock (the record's red collar and "one stock and clasp").

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever laid the stills beside the pictures; each checklist item is {what, status, note} with status open | reads | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling — open when a visitor would see the figure is not the pictures’ kind of person in that respect. The first figure of each role is the owner’s call (the plan’s "Your call"); later figures of the role are held to the one he approved. A reshoot of a changed figure (bound) sets the verdict back to unreviewed.
